subject: psychiatry
title: Trauma and stressor-related disorders

steps.tx: Exposure to threatened death, serious injury or sexual violence can produce trauma disorders through direct experience, witnessing or repeated occupational exposure. **Acute stress disorder** lasts from three days to one month with intrusion, dissociation, avoidance and arousal. **PTSD** persists beyond one month and includes intrusion, avoidance, negative cognition and mood and hyperarousal. Intrusion includes flashbacks and nightmares while hyperarousal includes hypervigilance, exaggerated startle and insomnia. Time course therefore separates acute stress disorder from **post traumatic stress disorder** in examination questions.
steps.say: Exposure to threatened death or sexual violence can produce trauma disorders afterwards. Acute stress disorder is present from three days to one month after trauma. PTSD is present beyond one month with intrusion, avoidance and hyperarousal features together. Intrusion is characterised by flashbacks and nightmares while hyperarousal is characterised by vigilance and insomnia.

steps.tx: **Adjustment disorder** describes emotional or behavioural symptoms that develop within three months of an identifiable stressor. Symptoms feel out of proportion to the stressor or impair function and resolve within six months after it ends. Clinicians do not diagnose adjustment disorder when another disorder explains the presentation better clinically. If full criteria for a **major depressive episode** are met, clinicians diagnose depression instead of adjustment disorder. Subtypes describe anxious mood, depressed mood, conduct disturbance or mixed features in patients.
steps.say: Adjustment disorder describes symptoms that develop within three months of a stressor. Symptoms affect function and resolve within six months after the stressor ends. Clinicians diagnose depression instead when full depressive episode criteria are met completely. Subtypes describe anxious mood, depressed mood or conduct disturbance in patients.

steps.tx: **Trauma focused CBT** and **EMDR** are first line treatments for PTSD and have the strongest supporting evidence. Clinicians offer therapy after stabilisation and help patients process traumatic memories in a controlled and paced manner. Single session debriefing should not be forced because it lacks benefit and may worsen symptoms. Antidepressant medicines or venlafaxine serve as second line treatment or adjuncts when therapy alone remains insufficient. **Benzodiazepines** worsen outcomes in PTSD and clinicians should avoid prescribing them for this disorder.
steps.say: Trauma focused CBT and EMDR are first line treatments for PTSD. Clinicians offer therapy after stabilisation and pace traumatic memory processing carefully during sessions. Single session debriefing should never be forced because benefit remains unproven clinically. Benzodiazepines worsen outcomes and clinicians should avoid prescribing them for PTSD.

The hierarchy ranks imaginal and real life tasks by distress so treatment proceeds step by step. Labels highlight **trauma focused CBT**, imaginal exposure, real life exposure and cognitive restructuring during the session. The calm setting matters because **graded exposure** works only when patients feel safe enough to stay engaged.

steps.tx: **Complex PTSD** develops after prolonged or repeated trauma such as childhood abuse, domestic captivity or ongoing violence. Patients show core PTSD symptoms plus disturbances in self organisation that affect daily functioning. These disturbances include affect dysregulation, negative self concept and persistent difficulty in relationships with others. Treatment follows **phase based care** with safety and stabilisation before trauma processing and later reintegration. Clinicians ensure current safety first and co treat depression, substance use and traumatic brain injury.
steps.say: Complex PTSD develops after prolonged trauma such as childhood abuse or captivity. Patients show affect dysregulation, negative self concept and persistent relationship difficulty together. Treatment follows phase based care with safety before trauma processing begins later. Clinicians make current safety the first priority and treat comorbid conditions alongside therapy.
